utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Nothing in the court agenda. No preliminaries have been announced. Therefore, we wait for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Jeremy will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dunjic.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please start by returning to the notebook entry that we left off with yesterday. That's 65 -- that's Exhibit P356. And if we could go to page 165.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, while that's being brought up, you'll recall that we were discussing a tour of the Igman Brigade by your commander. I think you said it was -- it was safe to assume that while you didn't recall that, that it would have been a tour by General Galic. Do you recall the purpose of that particular tour or tours such as this, even if you don't remember that exact tour?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: General Stanislav Galic toured my brigade on several occasions. Among other things, yesterday there was a question about who it was from the superior command because it was also General Mladic who toured my unit. Regarding what I was shown here, I can assume what it's all about; namely, the technical maintenance facility was one of the vital institutions and a key factor for the survival of the Serbian people in that territory. In a study by the director of the facility, I think it was Mr. Radivojsa, that was his last name, the facility was supposed to be transferred out of that area. My experience tells me, and I think that my action was correct, we prevented it from being transferred out because in combat it would take months and would affect the defensive capabilities of my unit and other units of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, I think we're jumping slightly ahead and we'll get to this point. In fact, if I introduce it, we see halfway down that page there is a reference to a discussion with this person whom you have referred to, this Colonel Radivojsa, and let's focus on that. We see that it says it's regarding the incident at the Hadzici TRZ, the maintenance and repairs depot. Now we see that there is a note stating Colonel Radivojsa's name and a reference to: "All disagreements began the moment the decision was taken to transfer part of the depot equipment to a new location in Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in the -- in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Next to the first star, we read: "On the morning of 31 October 1992, Radic walked in together with Major Dunjic, they arrested us pointing Heckler pistols at us." Now, this reference to Radic, that's President Radic who you referred to yesterday, the president of the municipality of Hadzici; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: The entry goes on to say: "Major Dunjic always came to the TRZ with Radic and he was always insolent and rude. "Major Dunjic treated the logistics people disparagingly, particularly General Djukic." Did you arrest Colonel Radivojsa on your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Radivojsa, let me correct you. Radivojsa. I didn't arrest him but I forbade any kind of relocation for the reasons that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you say you forbade any relocation. Did you forbid this on your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: In agreement with the political leadership. The relocation was not justified, for objective reasons. The relocation -- the depot was supposed to be relocated to Banja Luka. There was no reason for me to prevent the relocation other than the fact that I wanted to save the people in that area, and what confirmed that my decision was correct was the fact that in 1995, the people from Hadzici, when the depot was relocated, left that area. And that was one of the reasons why they left the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Referring to the people from Hadzici, we see further down in the same entry another reference, presumably there again Colonel Radivojsa's words. They say: "Everything that could be pillaged in Hadzici was pillaged by the Serbs and various militia." Now, Hadzici was in your zone of responsibility; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Hadzici was in my area of responsibility and the people who worked in the depot were from Hadzici and they worked in the depot before the war. There were no military formations in the depot at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And as brigade commander, you were aware of this pillage in Hadzici; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: What pillage?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: The pillage that we see referred to in this notebook entry of Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: What pillage? Could you please tell me what pillage? What was pillaged?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no laughter. No spoken or unspoken comments on questions or answers. You know the consequences if you continue. Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy. Well, Witness, Mr. Jeremy just read it, that the report says that everything that could be pillaged was pillaged. That is what Mr. Jeremy is referring to, whether you were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just a general assessment. Everything that was pillaged -- there was pillaged. This is not correct. Mrs. Plavsic later and the minister of defence, Mr. Subotic, toured the depot after these events, and the defence minister and she ascertained themselves that the depot was working to its full capacity according to all the regulations which satisfied all the criteria.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So just to understand your answer, you were not aware of any wide-scale pillaging in or outside that depot in the Hadzici area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you say that Mrs. Plavsic and the Minister of Defence, Mr. Subotic, later toured this depot. When did that -- when exactly did that tour occur?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: This was in late November. I don't recall the exact date, but what I say is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Let's take a look at another entry in this notebook. This time from the 14th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to e-court page 175 in the English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, we see this is an entry for Saturday the 14th of November 1992. We see the subheading: "Reporting by the Organs of the GS/Main Staff/ of the Army of RS/Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we could go to page 177, please. Two pages forward. Focusing in on number 4 that we see at the top of the page and the last starred asterisk.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: We see: "Order "Consider the possibility of appointing Lieutenant-Colonel Zeljaja commander of the Igman brigade." Mr. Dunjic, were you told by the Main Staff that in the middle of November 1992 they were considering replacing you as commander of the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't understand it like that. In November, I don't know the exact date, I wrote a request to the Main Staff that they should find another commander and that they should relieve me of duty because I disagreed with the way in which the defence of the Serbian people was organised in that section. I received an answer literally stating -- I received the answer from General Mladic: "Mr. Dunjic, kindly remain as commander of the Igman Brigade because the fighters believe in you, the Serbian people, and I myself also believe in you." After that, Mr. Galic came and asked me if I was going to stay. He probably later reported back that I would remain at that post, but at the time that's what happened regarding that. Otherwise, Mr. Mladic, I listened to him, because we have similar characteristics. We are officers. We are educated and trained. We do not tolerate injustice and unfit command, and above all we love the Serbian people, and we did everything to save the Serbian people in that area because it was easier to sacrifice an unfit colonel than lose tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, when you refer to the sacrifice of an unfit colonel, do I take it you're referring to Colonel Radivojsa?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Among others, yes. Him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And am I correct that you draw no connection to the arrest -- your arrest of Colonel Radivojsa that is noted in Mr. Mladic's diary and the discussion two days later about your replacement by Colonel Zeljaja?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: The translation is bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'll -- it's -- I'll phrase my question more clearly. Am I correct in thinking that when, on the 12th of November, we have an entry in Mr. Mladic's notebook referring to your arrest of Colonel Radivojsa, and then we see two days later a discussion about your replacement as commander of the Igman Brigade, am I correct in thinking that you draw no connection between those two events?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I didn't even know about it. I'm seeing for the first time that Mr. Zeljaja was supposed to take over the duty of commander. I wasn't informed of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And seeing this now, seeing this entry now, do you think it is connected to your decision, your decision that you took with the political authorities to arrest Colonel Radivojsa?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: It's possible. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on from here. Now, a few days after the events noted in these notebook entries we've looked at, do you recall attending a large meeting of political and military figures who were operating in the area of the SRK? The meeting was held at the Lukavica barracks.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to take a look at the minutes of those meetings and ask you a few questions in relation to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, I'm slightly confused, Mr. Dunjic. Earlier you said you didn't arrest Mr. Radivojsa, and later now you were asked -- you explained that by saying that you just prevented any relocation. Did you mean relocation of the depot or did you mean relocation of anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the relocation of the maintenance and repair depot, and I didn't arrest Colonel Radivojsa. I just expelled him. Got him out of there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "expelled him"? In factual terms, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ordered him to leave the area of responsibility of my brigade and that area included the maintenance and repairs depot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And did he follow your order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy. My confusion, by the way, was caused by -- later on whether the arrest was connected with or was not connected, linked with the other matter. And if there was no arrest, it's difficult for someone to tell us whether there is any link between something that didn't happen and something that is referred to at a later entry in the notebook. Just for you to know what caused my confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please see P1967.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Those are the minutes of the meeting that I just asked you about, Mr. Dunjic. As this is being brought up, I can tell you that these are the minutes of the SRK corps command from a meeting of commanders and presidents operating in the political and military situation in the SRK zone, dated 15 November 1992. So on the first page we see the date is 15 November 1992, and so that's a day after the notebook entry that indicated consideration was being given to replacing you as commander of the Igman Brigade. We see a list of persons present at the start of the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to page 2 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S, please. Now, number 29 we see a reference to Velimir Dunjic, Igman Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So that's a reference to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: On the next page in the English, same page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: We read: "On behalf of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army, the following were present: "- Commander, Colonel General Ratko Mladic and "- Colonel Tolimir."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, could we go to page 5 in the English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now looking at the top of the page in the B/C/S and halfway down the page in the English, we see that an introductory report is submitted by Lieutenant-Colonel Marko Lugonja. Mr. Dunjic, he was the commander -- the assistant commander of intel and security in the SRK; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd like to look at some of the aspects of the report that he provides to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we can go to e-court page 7 in the English and 6 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And looking at the subheading on that page, we see that he is giving a report on basic security issues in SRK units.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 8 in the English and 7 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of the page in the English, I think at the top of the page in the B/C/S, we see a reference to: "Creation of formal and informal groups and organisations gathering around an already prominent and credible individual. They exercise a status in units by threats, extortion, and other violent methods."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lugonja's report continues, and he references: "Extremely widespread theft, robbery, violence and other crimes." He goes on to describe various things being stolen. And in the next hyphen point we see he states: "The understanding and practice of individuals and groups that they are masters of life and death to every individual of different ethnicity, resulting in cases of unnecessary mistreatment and killing of members of other ethnicities, especially Muslims. Such people see the Geneva and other conventions as obsolete and unnecessary in this war." Now, Mr. Dunjic, I put it to you that one of the groups that Lieutenant-Colonel Lugonja is referring to here is Branislav Gavrilovic's unit which was under your command.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I assert that that is not correct. You need to give me evidence that the group committed any crimes during the time that I was commander. And the group that you are speaking of, you showed me a document yesterday in which my successor, Spasoje Cojic, confirmed to -- issued a certificate, proof to Branislav Gavrilovic, that he was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska or a member of the Army of Republika Srpska. I'm saying that he was in the army and my successor confirmed that in writing. Not that he was a member of the paramilitary units but a member of the Army of Republika Srpska. You showed me that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Dunjic, from your answer, I understand your evidence to be that you were not aware of any crimes committed by Gavrilovic's unit during the time that you were commander of the Igman Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: In my statement, I stated that as far as I know, Branislav Gavrilovic's unit, while I was in command, did not commit any crimes, did not do anything that would contravene the provisions of the Geneva Conventions. And now whether there were any minor disciplinary breaches, whether there were fights or things like that, I don't know. I didn't really care that much because that unit accounted for 2.5 per cent of the complement of my brigade, so I focused in my work on the others. Like any other commander of any other unit in the world, I didn't focus on just a 2.5 per cent -- a complement of my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Let's take a look at another document in connection with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see P04595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so. You were present at that meeting, it was, apparently -- you said it was the Gavrilovic unit did not commit any crimes. What was the -- what was hinted at when there was talk about widespread theft, killing? Did you understand what they were talking about or was it totally unknown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This report does not relate to my brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lugonja was the chief of security in the corps, so this refers to corps units. I was the one who prevented plunder, looting, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this happened by corps units. Could you explain to us what exactly then which units committed -- which corps units committed those crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know that. This is just a sweeping generalisation. There are no facts as to what happened and if it did, where it happened. I don't know if you understand me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if there are made such sweeping statements not specifically referring to corps units but in very general terms and insisting on measures to be taken, that you at least asked where this happened and by whom this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not the one who was supposed to ask those questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was -- you were not -- your units were not excluded from the sweeping statements, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that that had nothing to do with my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For what reason did you think that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I tried to keep everything under control in my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have the impression that any of your colleagues did not try to do the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was my impression. And subsequent events would prove that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Which colleagues then were not doing the same; that is, trying to prevent these type of crimes to be committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only the perpetrators of crimes but also they proved to be incapable of organise combat, especially the Rajlovac and -- Rajlovac and Vogosca Brigade were of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not interested in combat. You said it was your impression that the others did not do the same as you did, that is, to prevent crimes. My question was whom of your colleagues, in your impression, did not try to prevent crimes to be committed? Crimes as theft, large-scale theft, and killing of other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the killing of members of other ethnicities, I knew nothing about that. And if you're talking about theft and plunder, we're not talking about the robbing of Muslims and Croats. Those were internal problems in the territory under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's not what the report describes. You told us that you did not feel that you were addressed by the sweeping statements because you tried to prevent these type of crimes - that is, large-scale theft, killing of people of other ethnicity - that others did not try to prevent that. You did, and therefore it didn't address you. I'm asking you whom of your colleagues did not prevent the type of crimes as described in this report? And now you are moving to combat. I didn't ask about combat. You're moving to internal little problems. I'm not talking about that. I'm talking about the type of crimes as described in what Mr. Lugonja reported. Whom of your colleagues did not prevent those crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That question - i.e., who did not prevent crimes - should be put to the author of this information. Not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'm telling you that according to what I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that it was my impression that my colleagues did not do what I did; that is, to prevent these type of crimes. My question is: Whom did you have in mind when you said that you had the impression that the others did not do the same and, as you said, which later turned out to be really the truth? Who of your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commands of the Rajlovac and Vogosca Brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember their names. Perhaps Mr. -- I apologise, it was 22 years ago. In any case, the commanders of those units. I'm sure you have the names of those persons who were in command during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, how did it become apparent from later events that they did not try to prevent these crimes to be committed? What did you have in mind when you told us that this turned out to be the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was an operation during which they were arrested, and they were arrested primarily - and that was the foremost reason - due to their incapability to organise combat. They were very --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not talking about combat. You told us that following events showed that they did not sincerely try to prevent these crimes to be committed. I ask you, what are these events that happened later on that demonstrated that your colleague commanders did not do their utmost best to prevent these crimes, large-scale theft, killings of other ethnicities, were committed? What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't repeat anything you said before. Please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know that people committed crimes any of the brigades. I didn't know that. Why don't you put that question to Mr. Lugonja? I'm sure that he will be able to tell you exactly who he meant. I'm not the best suited person for that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you. You said, "It was not me who was addressed by it because I did everything to prevent these type of crimes." I then asked you was that different for your colleagues? You said, "Yes, I had the impression that the others did not sincerely try to prevent that which was shown by later events." That's what you told us, not what Mr. Lugonja told us. And I'm asking you a clarification, and I unfortunately have to establish that you're evasive in your answers in this respect. Mr. Jeremy, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you still want to answer my last question, then you have an opportunity to do so; that is, what events demonstrated that your colleagues did not sincerely try to prevent these crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This information that we can see here does not relate only to killings and theft. There are other things here. There are other missions in the work of those people as described here. If you allow me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you to clarify some of your previous answers, and you're moving away from my questions again and again. I gave you an opportunity to answer my last question. You didn't do so. Mr. Jeremy will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please see P04595.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Dunjic, while this is being brought to the screen, I can tell you it's a report from SRK commander General Galic to the Main Staff, dated 18 November 1992; therefore, a few days after the meeting we've just been discussing. In point --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Just to show you, Mr. Dunjic, that it's signed by General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we can go back to the first page now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: In point number 1, we see a reference to enemy operations and some description. In point number 2, we see a reference to "operation by our forces." I'd like to focus your attention, Mr. Dunjic, on point number 3, where we read the following: "The situation in the territory without significant changes. However, a paramilitary formation consisting of about 25 men commanded by Branislav Gavrilovic, aka Brne, is active in the Rakovica sector. This is a group of criminals whose behaviour is damaging the reputation of the Republika Srpska Army in the eyes of the population in this territory." Now, Mr. Dunjic, you agree that the Branislav Gavrilovic being referred to here is a reference to the same Commander Gavrilovic who was under your command at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And on the basis of the answers that you've given me saying that you knew of no crimes that Gavrilovic committed during the time that you were commander of the Igman Brigade, how is it that the -- the commander of the SRK, who you have told us yesterday commanded up to 25.000 troops, is aware of crimes being committed by Gavrilovic and his men but that you were not. How can that be the case?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: First of all, this is another general assessment, and that includes the number of men in the units. This seems to me like an assessment of the artistic impression in skating. There is no evidence whatsoever. It just says, "This is a group of criminals." This is a sweeping description. As a commander, I was not interested in who was what before the war, or after the war for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, we see that Mr. Galic is specific in terms of the unit he refers to. It's Gavrilovic's unit. We see he is specific in terms of the area in which that unit is committing crimes. So it's not a general assessment. In fact, it's actually quite specific. So how is it that General Galic had this specific information despite the fact that he was responsible for eight times as many soldiers as you were but it's your evidence that you did not have information about crimes being committed by Mr. Gavrilovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Obviously you don't understand certain things in here. Gavrilovic's unit was deployed in Rakovica in the orchard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please focus on the question. The question is: Why was General Galic reporting about misbehaviour of Gavrilovic's unit, where you, being -- commanding the brigade say you had no knowledge of it? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know anything about that. If I had known, I would have taken measures. I did not. I did not report on things like that in my reports. Now, as to how he received that information, by what parallel channels of information, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Dunjic, it's your evidence that while we see Mr. Galic reporting to the Main Staff his concerns about crimes being committed by a unit under your command, you're saying that Mr. Galic's concerns were never brought to your attention in your capacity as commander of the Igman Brigade. Is that how I should understand your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Don't say that. What crimes are mentioned in this report? The only thing that is mentioned is that they are a group of criminals whose behaviour among the population, I suppose that the reference is made to the Serbian population, tarnishes the reputation of the army of Republika Srpska. This is what I am reading. So the operative word is "behaviour" or "conduct."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, there is a clear reference to Gavrilovic's unit being "a group of criminals." Is it your evidence that you -- that General Galic never brought to your attention that he considered this unit under your brigade to be a group of criminals. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: It's a very serious qualification when somebody says of other people that they are a group of criminals. I don't remember that -- Galic ever told me any such thing. I am not an investigating judge. I did not ask for my soldiers' criminal records. I never investigated whether any of them had been convicted of crimes before the war. That was never my intention or my task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the report - and you are consistently ignoring certain aspects of it - is not only about being a bunch of criminals but also about problematic behaviour linked in the text of this report directly to it being a group of criminals with problematic behaviour. Were you never informed about the problematic behaviour of this group described by General Galic as a group of criminals when they were under your command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I have already told you that I don't remember that he ever informed about that. Second of all, whether people behaved in this way or another way was less important than the organisation of combat. It was really not important whether somebody had beaten somebody else in a restaurant. That was not what I concerned myself with in my work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you did not link this information you may have received and you said you were not interested in, you did not link that to the observations made during that consultation meeting about widespread theft and murder? You did not think is the one perhaps related to the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no murders in my brigade. I did not receive this information. It was sent to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the same. You say there were no murders or do you say I don't know of murders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that there were none. None committed by the unit or individuals in it. I didn't know. I think that there weren't in. I'm even sure that there weren't any while I was the commander of the Igman Brigade. If I'd known of a murder, I'm certain that such a case would have been prosecuted without any second thoughts about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just now to summarise: You attended a meeting where Lugonja stated that widespread theft and killing on an ethnical basis happened, and you thought, well, he's addressing someone else. Asked who else he may have addressed, you're evasive in your answers. We now see that General Galic is reporting to the Main Staff that a group of criminals is showing behaviour which is, to say the least, problematic, and you still say, well, what may have happened, I was more interested in combat and I did not directly receive a report, so I assume that no such crimes under my command happened. That seems to be the gist of your testimony. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You understood me well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says in this report that there were murders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not you who are asking the questions. I didn't say that in this report it was said that murders were committed, so don't put that question to me. Mr. Stojanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, in order to avoid confusion, we were listening to the interpretation and you were interpreted as saying that Mr. Lugonja reported that all those crimes were ethnically based. In the text showed to the witness by the Prosecutor, that part - and I'm referring the ethnically based crimes - are actually not what Mr. Lugonja said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think -- but we could check that. I think that he referred to feeling that someone is the master of another's life and the ethnicity is clearly mentioned there, Mr. Stojanovic, isn't it, in the portion we saw earlier? Especially the Muslims were mentioned specifically in this meeting where Mr. Lugonja spoke. If you say it doesn't appear there, then please take me back to that part of the report of this meeting where Lugonja is speaking and indicate to me that no reference so ethnicity was made and I'll be glad to agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are -- we saw document P1967.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we are close to the break. If you would perhaps briefly meet with Mr. Jeremy during the break and find where I misstated the evidence in this respect, and please then put that to me in detail before the witness enters the courtroom, and I'll be glad to look at it and to listen to it. Judge Moloto has one question before we take the break -- Judge Fluegge, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, earlier today you said Mr. Gavrilovic was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In this document we have still on the screen, the report, the regular combat report of your superior commander, it is said: "The situation in the territory without significant changes. However, a paramilitary formation consisting of about 25 men commanded by Branislav Gavrilovic ...," and so on. He is addressed here as a commander of a paramilitary formation. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't. It says here that their behaviour is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In his information, Lugonja even characterises their behaviour as criminal behaviour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop. I asked you something else. Was he commander of a paramilitary formation or was he a member of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was not a member of a paramilitary formation. To prove that, you saw a document yesterday where Mr. Cojic confirms in writing that he was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska in the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you saying that your commander was wrong in writing that, that he made a mistake or he was misleading or he was lying? Are you saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a problem. At the beginning of the war, there was a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If somebody's name was Savo Derikonja he was immediately considered a paramilitary or if he was a member of party, he was considered to be a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- paramilitary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was done automatically and it was not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 18th of November 1992. Your commander addressed Gavrilovic as a commander of a paramilitary unit. Was that correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct that that's what he called him, but the -- that was not correct. You saw a payroll and you saw that that unit was on the strength of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you still saying that your commander made a mistake or was misleading the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that he made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you may follow the usher. We take a break of 20 minutes. We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with the witness. Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber received half an hour ago the message that Mr. Bukva would not be ready to come and testify because proofing or preparation is not completed yet. The Chamber does not understand why a witness, who was interviewed last time on the 27th of June, who signed his statement on the 18th of July of this year, who arrived in The Hague, and where there was an opportunity yesterday to continue to prepare him, where there was more time this morning to continue to prepare him, could not be available once we've done with this witness. And therefore, the Chamber is seriously considering, if Mr. Lukic doesn't appear and if the witness doesn't appear at the end of the testimony of the present witness, that we'll consider whether this is time lost for the Defence. It's totally unclear why you need more than five or six hours. In these circumstances, Mr. Lukic himself having been present during the interviews, as we read that, why we couldn't just continue. Another reason might be that it was at the request of Mr. Lukic yesterday that we postponed the evidence of the previous witness, and the Chamber is aware that the Defence blames the Chamber for the inability to hear the testimony of that witness but does not necessarily agree with that point of view, and considers that at least there is a serious part of responsibility for the Defence as well. But apart from all that, five or six hours, under the present circumstances, should be enough to call this witness and to examine him. Would you please pass this message to Mr. Lukic, inclusive that the Chamber will consider whether this time not used will be deducted from the time available for the Defence. Can the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I further inquire, not to pursue the matter at this very moment, but whether Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Jeremy you sat together and have established that there was no reference to ethnicity, or if you have any observations in this respect then I'd like to hear later from you, perhaps at the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, I have a final question on the topic that we were discussing at the time end of the last session, and it is this: It is correct, is it not, that you never took any disciplinary action against Branislav Gavrilovic or any of the men in his unit?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I think that is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move on and take a look at your -- the statement that you provided for this particular case. The additional statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And that's D599. If we could have that on our screens, please. If we could go to the -- to the next page in each of the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Dunjic, I'm particularly interested in paragraph 4 in the statement. It's now up on the screen. And there you refer to the fact that in early December 1992 you state: "I was designated pursuant to an order of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps (SRK) Command, signed by the Chief of Staff Colonel Dragan Marcetic to co-ordinate the command and control of the Rajlovac and Ilidza Brigades in addition to my duties as the Commander of the Igman Brigade." Mr. Dunjic, you recall this particular assignment you refer to in paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. I received a written order on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you a document in connection with that assignment and I'll ask you a few questions on that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 09808.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, while this is being brought to our screens, I'll tell you it's an SRK report to the Main Staff of the VRS. It's dated 16 December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we could go to the last page, please, in the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we see it's type signed by Ljubljana Kosovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the first page in English and B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that, in your quote, Mr. Jeremy, the Rajlovac Brigade is mentioned but not the Ilidza Brigade. Rajlovac and Ilidza Brigade in addition to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, in paragraph 3 on page 1 of this report, we read: "At the moment, the most critical situation is in the area of the municipality of Rajlovac and Vogosca."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we go to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we read in the second paragraph: "In the areas of the municipalities of Hadzici, Ilidza, Rajlovac, and Vogosca, the chief organiser of the paramilitary formations is Major Dunjic, the commander of the Blazuj Brigade." Now, Mr. Dunjic, the command post of your Igman Brigade was in Blazuj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And the Major Dunjic being referred to here is you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, the report goes on to say: "He is discharging the duties of brigade commander in form only. He fails to show up at the brigade for three days at a time. He has unified under his command paramilitary formations and some special forces units; he is supplying them with weapons and ammunition; he has taken out all the combat equipment from the repair and maintenance depot and placed it at the disposal of these formations. It is clear now why he had expelled the Depot management." And that expelling of the depot management is a reference to the entry in General Mladic's notebook we saw earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct. Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now if we go to the next paragraph, we read: "Noting all the seriousness of such a situation, the Corps Command sent Colonel Kosovac, Assistant Commander for Morale, and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic" --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I think we need to go to the next page in the B/C/S, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lieutenant-Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. "Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic to Rajlovac on 8 December 1992 to assist in consolidating the situation ..." Did that in fact happen?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the corps commands did send them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: And then after that I was appointed co-ordinator.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take a look at the next paragraph. It states: "Dissatisfied with the general situation and with the endangered state of this part of the front, supposedly with the approval of the Presidency, various municipal leaders take the decision to have the commands of the Rajlovac and Vogosca Brigade arrested; the one executing this was Major Dunjic and his people. In addition ... the commands of the brigades, Colonel Kosovac" -- excuse me. "In addition to the commands of the brigades, Colonel Kosovac and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic were arrested, also." Mr. Dunjic, you don't deny that in September 1992 you were in Rajlovac and you arrested Colonel Kosovac and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic; correct? Excuse me, in December 1992.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I don't deny. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you, in making these arrests, men from Branislav Gavrilovic's unit, acted together with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you an excerpt of your testimony in that case where a similar question was put to you, and I'd like to show you the answer that you provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Can we please see 65 ter 31115. And I would like to go to page 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now focusing on line 17, you were asked a question -- or I'll read it to you and it will be translated. So the question was, and this was by -- this was during the cross-examination, so by Prosection counsel. The question was: "Now, sir, you don't deny in September 1992 you were in the Zuc area and you made some arrests; correct?" And you state: "Well, I denied that I was at Zuc. I mean, I was below Zuc. Let us be precise. I was in Rajlovac. And it is correct that I arrested Colonel Kosovac and Lieutenant-Colonel Maljkovic, and it is correct that I arrested almost the entire municipality of Rajlovac. And I think that that was a brilliant move in order to save tens of thousands of Serb people. "Q. Let's speak specifically about who went along with you. This" --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the next page or is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: It's not the next page. Is that the next page in e-court? It should be 30509. Could we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the correct page. And if we could go to one page back so I can regain the continuity of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, the -- it's difficult to go back again. You will lose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's 511 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. So the question, 30511, last line.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: "Q. Let us speak specifically about who went along with you."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: If we could just go one page forward, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: "This talks about your men. Were these men from Brne's unit who were with you? "A. Part of them, yes." So, Mr. Dunjic, in your Karadzic testimony, you state that Gavrilovic's men, Brne's men, were with you when you made these arrests. Now you stated that they were not with you. So which is correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Let me explain. May I? The unit and other units from the brigade were at Zuc in view of the fact that those positions were falling. The unit was at the following position, the position named Smetliste. That was Gavrilovic's unit. It was there in order to prevent the enemy from breaking through, but it was not only at Rajlovac when Kosovac and Maljkovic were arrested from the Rajlovac municipality. And that is the correct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, I'm a little confused. Were Brne's men with you or were they not with you when you made those arrests?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: They were not with me during that arrest. They were at the Smetliste facility and they were arresting a lieutenant there who was running away from the line. We are talking about two different arrests here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And so when in the Karadzic case you talk about making these arrests, you talk about it being a brilliant move, you were asked who went along with you and you said -- and you were asked were men from Brne's unit with you, and you said yes. You're now saying that in fact you were not referring to the particular arrest but a separate operation. Is that how I understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: They were with me in Rajlovac in the area of responsibility of the brigade, but they were not with me at the brigade command when that arrest was carried out. They were at positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I try to find out. You're talking about a series of arrests including the arrest of Kosovac and Maljkovic, and you considered them together as one brilliant action. In that brilliant action, arresting several people, were Brne's men assisting you, were they involved in those arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not take part in those arrests because they were at positions in the area of responsibility of the Rajlovac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Karadzic testimony suggests otherwise. Not that they were at combat positions but part of the unit, that's a very specific answer. Part of the unit was with you when arrests were made. Which part of the unit was with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The special police units from Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now but not from Brne? Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not Brne. People from Brne's unit were not with me at the Rajlovac command. You're asking me for very much detail. They did not ask for so many details in the previous trial. If they had, I would have explained. That's why I said partly, partly because they were in a different position. They were deployed elsewhere in the area of responsibility of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I specifically asked about the arrests in the Karadzic case, and it was read to you a minute ago, who were with you. This talk about your men. Were these men from Brne's unit who was with you? And you were talking about the arrests. You said: "Part of them, yes." My question is which part of Brne's men did you refer to at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The troops that were deployed in that position. I took several units to Rajlovac in order to prevent the fall of those positions. Those units were from the Igman Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, this answer was given in direct connection with you involving -- being involved in arrests. To say that they were somewhere on their positions is inconsistent with your testimony given in the Karadzic case. Do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in Rajlovac. There is nothing in dispute about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But they were not with me during the arrests. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard you saying that and I put it to you that it's inconsistent with what you said in the Karadzic case and I asked for an explanation, not for you to repeat what you said already several times. Do you have an explanation for this inconsistency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My possible explanation would be that the Prosecutor didn't ask for so much detail. If I said they were in Rajlovac, he thought that they were with me. They were in Rajlovac but not with me during the arrest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will carefully read the testimony in the Karadzic case and see whether your explanation assists us. Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you gave the order to make these arrests; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you gave this order without first consulting your superior officers; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to go back and take a look at this same report that we were looking at a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we again look at 65 ter 09808. Can we go to the second page in the B/C/S, please, and second page in the English please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, five or so paragraphs from the end, we read: "There was" -- At the bottom of the page in the English, we read: "There was no excuse for the arrests of complete commands of the brigades ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: In the next sentence, we read: "The Brigades were thereby left completely leaderless at the moment of the strongest enemy offensive. The next day, Colonel Marcetic, the Corps Chief of Staff, was also the target of abuse." Mr. Dunjic, this Colonel Marcetic is the person you refer to in paragraph 4 of your statement, the person that actually appointed you to oversee these brigades; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same Colonel Marcetic, the chief of the corps staff. He was not ill-treated. He was not in Rajlovac. As far as I know, he was in a Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: We read continuing on: "During the execution of these operations, there was theft and looting of military property." Witness, in this document it says that various municipal leaders take the decision to have the commands of the Rajlovac and Vogosca Brigade arrested. Was there any involvement of municipal leaders in the decision to arrest those brigade commands? Now you don't deny that there was theft and looting of military property, do you?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I deny the looting of property. I did this to prevent the fall of the entire defence line and prevent any possible cases of looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender that document as the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 09808 receives number P6705, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Actually, forgive me. Could we take a final look at P6705. The document we were just looking at. I've got a question on the final paragraph of that document. It's still on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Dunjic, the last paragraph in this document reads as follows: "Also, we propose that Major Dunjic be immediately relieved of his duties, arrested, and that criminal proceedings be instituted for exceeding his authority and refusing to obey Corps Command orders." So, Mr. Dunjic, again we see in December there is another suggestion that you should be replaced as brigade commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Please, this report was drafted by a colonel whom I arrested, the same man from Kos was arrested and he drafted this report only two days later. You should have checked that. I still believe that that was an excellent move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether here, whomever did it, suggested you to be replaced as a brigade commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't receive this document. It was not addressed at me. I was not aware of it at all. I was appointed as co-ordinator, and I was not removed from my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, the Chamber is able to read what this document says. The witness says he has no knowledge of it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, despite the fact that you didn't see this document at the time, did it come to your attention in December 1992 that again your replacement was being discussed and, in this case, suggested?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, no. I was appointed as a co-ordinator.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And after appointed being -- after being appointed co-ordinator and making these arrests, it was never brought to your attention that because of the way you executed your duties, your replacement was being represented to the Main Staff. You're saying that never came to your attention?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that anybody said anything. However, the result of that operation was this: We prevented the fall of those municipalities, we reinforced our defence, and we saved the Serbian population in that area. In view of the fact that any municipality or the sector of any the brigades west of Sarajevo would cause a domino effect. It would have a ripple effect on the entire territory and the entire territory would have been lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. So nobody told you in December that they were planning or suggesting that you be replaced as Igman Brigade commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now in January 1993 in the next month --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, before you continue, I have a few questions still related to December and this document for the witness. Witness, in this document it says that various municipal leaders take the decision to have the commands of the Rajlovac and Vogosca Brigade arrested. Was there any involvement of municipal leaders in the decision to arrest those brigade commands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of that decision. No, I don't know. I made it myself for Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now it's also said in this document that this decision was supposedly taken with the approval of the presidency. Did you have any contact with the presidency in relation to this action, arresting the brigade commands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have any contacts. The brigade -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you acted purely on your own without any orders from the corps level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was a matter of minutes whether the positions would fall or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you -- I asked you about the reference to Colonel Marcetic in that document and you said that no harm came to Colonel Marcetic.

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is not what I said. I said that he was not in Rajlovac. I think that he was in Vogosca, but I don't know what transpired there. I didn't say that he -- no harm had come to him. I only said that he was not in Rajlovac but that he was in Vogosca as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So you said that he was not ill-treated. He was not in Rajlovac. So is it your testimony he was not ill-treated in Rajlovac but it may be he was ill-treated elsewhere, you just don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know about that because he was not in Rajlovac. I don't know what happened in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you were replaced in January 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the order of the corps command. I don't know whether the corps was relevant or not. However, I was removed, I obeyed the order, and I left the area of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Until the very end of the war, I had no further contacts with the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now it's correct, isn't it, that on hearing about the decision, on being told a decision had been made to replace you, you had an altercation with General Galic; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. The decision on my dismissal followed the incident involving General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to show you a document in connection with the incident with General Galic and I'd ask you some questions on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see 65 ter 31126.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And this is an Official Note from the RS MUP. Now, Mr. Dunjic, referring to this document, we see it reads in the -- on the third line: "On 14 January 1993 in the afternoon, General Galic came to Hadzici to visit the commander of Igman Brigade, Major Velimir Dunjic. The two met in the Dunjic's flat in the presence of some company commanders and fighters who had also been invited. The meeting lasted until late. Alcohol was consumed. Some were already under the influence. At about midnight that day, General Galic and Major Dunjic started disagreeing. At one point Major Dunjic jumped up and rip off the general's ranks from his camouflage uniform and dipped them into some gravy sauce" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where are we exactly in the text? Could you guide us, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Forgive me, Your Honours. I've have been reading from a related but different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we'd like to follow the document you showed to us on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I understand. Can we please see 65 ter 31125.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, I've read to you the second and third paragraphs of the document on the screen before you. I continue from where I left off: "General Galic didn't react. After some heavy arguing and alcohol consumption, a physical confrontation between Galic and Dunjic broke out." So it's correct, Mr. Dunjic, that in January 1993 you actually got into a physical confrontation with your corps commander, General Galic; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And it was as a consequence of this confrontation that you were removed from your role as commander of the Igman Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose that that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And do you dispute the events described in this MUP document we see on the screen before us?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I deny that in the part where it says that I was under the influence. I'm talking about myself. Second of all, I dispute that Brne's men were involved. While I was the brigade commander, Brne never entered the command post where I was in command, where I was in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm lost now. I don't see anything about Brne in this document and I don't know what the witness is talking about at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And secondly, he just -- you just agreed, Mr. Dunjic, a few minutes ago that as a consequence of the incidents described here, you were dismissed. Now suddenly you deny them. Can you please explain yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not deny the fact that I was dismissed after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you are denying the incidents described in this document after you have admitted that it was a consequence of these incidents that caused your dismissal. Listen to my question. Do you have an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the question was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was you'd just admitted a few minutes ago that as a consequence of the events that are described in this document, you were dismissed. Now, on a subsequent question, you are now saying you deny that the incidents described in this document took place. And then you want to bring -- you want to say you were not under the influence. There is no mention of you being under the influence here and that is not Mr. Jeremy's question. Only said here about alcohol is that it was consumed, by who we don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not saying that I was not dismissed after the incident and that that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not my --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that may have been the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not denying that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop. That was not the question. You did admit that you were dismissed but you also did admit that the reason you were dismissed was because of the incidents described in this document. Now, how do you then come to say, and I want you to explain this inconsistency, that you deny the events that took place in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not denying that the incident took place, but I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- disputing the entire description of the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was my question. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have, perhaps, then a few questions. Apparently you say an incident happened but not in the way described here. You referred to Brne's men. We've talked about them quite a bit. Were any of those of Gavrilovic's unit present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there any fighters present other than Gavrilovic's men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my security detail, which secured the command post, and General Galic's escorts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were in the flat where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the flat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did any of your security detail ever belonged to a unit which was commanded by Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at that time or before that. As a matter of fact, I don't know. While I was in command none of the people who were at the command post -- no, no, no, nobody was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether any of your security detail had been a member of Gavrilovic's unit at whatever point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Not before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other document shown from which Mr. Jeremy was not quoting specifically mentions the presence of Brne's Chetniks during this party, and you say that's just invented. It's not true. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any company commanders present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you say you don't remember, apparently you do not remember the exact composition of the company that was present in the flat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to remember that because it was the permanent security detail that provided security for the command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I asked you about company commanders, you said I don't remember. So apparently you're not fully acquainted anymore with who were and who were not present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that members of my security detail were there as well as members of Galic's security detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether any company commanders were present. Your response was: "I don't remember. I don't know. I don't think so." This led me to my question that you may not remember the presence -- remember all those who were present or were not present. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was well understood. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, do you dispute that you ripped off General Galic's ranks from his camouflage uniform or is that part of the report correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That did in fact happen; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It did happen. When General Galic ordered members of his security detail to shoot at me, I ripped off his ranks because he already invoked his authority as a general. He said he could do whatever. And that's when he ordered his security detail to shoot at me, then I ripped off his ranks, and I told him, "Now we can talk as two human beings without any ranks."

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And what prompted General Galic to order members of his security detail to shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: We were at a meeting in Ilidza. Mr. Morillon was there as well as Mr. Galic and myself. We discussed a celebration of rank awarding to Mr. Galic and to Mr. Morillon. After the official part of the meeting, there was a cocktail party which I left, that was the unofficial part, and I left and went to my command post in Hadzici. In the evening, Galic and his security detail arrived there. He was angry with me for having left the cocktail party where alcohol had been consumed, and he was also angry that I had arrested people in Rajlovac including Colonels Kosovac and Maljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender that document as the next Prosecution exhibit, 31125.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31125 receives number P6706, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we just have another look at 31126. It was on our screens before this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, I'm calling up a document you've already had an opportunity to look at. It's an RS report dated the 18th of January, 1993. It relates to the same incident. You've actually described a number of the events described in this particular document. We see in the first paragraph that there is a reference to Brne's men being present in the apartment. I understand that your evidence is that that was not the case; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is not correct. That's why I said that Brne's men were not there, because I already saw this document before it was shown to me and I reacted immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now just before we leave this document, I'd like to direct your attention to the final paragraph where we read: "We have information that within the military circles in the area of Hadzici, Ilidza, and Butila, there is talk that on that occasion the general was arrested, and as a reason for that, his sacking of Major Dunjic from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps is cited." Is it correct that the reason you assaulted General Galic was because you, and the reason that he asked his men to shoot at you, is because you tried to arrest him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. You would have had the exact data on that even now, 22 years after the fact, had he actually been arrested. Mr. Galic did not see me nor did he sack me. The procedure is quite different in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Did you attempt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question was whether you were shot at because you'd tried to arrest General Galic. I think your answer is that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dunjic, you've mentioned your security detail. Could you tell me the name of the person who was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: VELIMIR DUNJIC
utterances.text: I think that it was Dragan Kecanovic, Dragan Kecanovic. He was a member of the special units of the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP before the war. And Krstic, Krstic, Krstic -- I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender that document as the next Prosecution exhibit.
